[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Give the artifact store a lifecycle - report, dry-run pruning, and [/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]         [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]opt-in retention[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]The artifact-file store can be measured, drained, and bounded: [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]`sase artifact stats` reports its economics, `sase artifact prune` [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]and `sase artifact reclaim` are dry-run by default and route every [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]removal through a restorable trash, an opt-in `artifacts.retention`[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]policy keeps the store bounded going forward, and nothing an agent [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]declared or a bead, plan, or ChangeSpec references is ever removed.[/#D7D7AF]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Rust core: store economics, retention planner, and trash [/bold #D7AFFF]     [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]primitives[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]core-lifecycle[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]

    [#D7D7AF]planner, and clock-free trash store/list/restore/purge primitives to [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`sase_core`, expose all four through `sase_core_rs`, and release the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]crate.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Store economics report and the protected-reference scan[/bold #D7AFFF]       [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]py-report[dim] · [dim][/dim]after core-lifecycle[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]py-report: raise the `sase-core-rs` pin, add the Python bridges for [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]economics and retention planning, add the bead/plan/ChangeSpec reference[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]scan that produces protected artifact ids, and ship `sase artifact [/#D7D7AF]

[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Dry-run-first pruning and the trash lifecycle[/bold #D7AFFF]                 [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]py-prune[dim] · [dim][/dim]after py-report[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]py-prune: add `sase artifact prune` (dry run unless `--apply`) and the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`sase artifact trash {list,purge,restore}` group, with index-row removal[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and restoration performed under the existing index lock and every [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]removal routed through the trash.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Retroactive version-control reclaim of the pooled bytes[/bold #D7AFFF]       [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]py-reclaim[dim] · [dim][/dim]after py-prune[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]py-reclaim: add `sase artifact reclaim`, which converts stored automatic[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]rows whose exact content is reproducible from a durable ref into [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]byte-free VCS-backed rows and trashes the redundant copies, reusing the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]capture policy's git probe and verifying by digest first.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Opt-in retention configuration and enforcement[/bold #D7AFFF]                [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]

    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
